title: CXMT fifth-generation DRAM platform and 24Gb LPDDR5X enter mass production
observed_evidence: CXMT announced at the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention that its fifth-generation DRAM technology platform has entered mass production.

CXMT said the platform reduces the active-area half-pitch to 11.95 nm using quadruple patterning and can produce at least 50% more gross dies per wafer than its fourth-generation platform on an 8Gb baseline; gross dies are not equivalent to tested-good yield.
CXMT unveiled two 24Gb LPDDR5X products made on the new platform and said both are already in mass production for smartphone and portable-device applications.

Nanya Technology's current product catalogue includes LPDDR5/5X, establishing direct product-category overlap; no claim is made here about customer displacement, realized market share, pricing changes or Nanya shipment loss.
semantic_interpretation: This is a newly materialized competitive-supply catalyst for Nanya Technology rather than a deterministic financial-data update. CXMT's move from development to mass production in LPDDR5X increases medium-term competitive and pricing risk in a product category Nanya is developing and commercializing. The near-term impact is uncertain because CXMT did not disclose tested-good yield, shipment volume, customer allocation, ASP or global share, and Nanya's demand mix includes other DRAM and AI/custom products. Treat as competitive pressure, not as evidence of an immediate Nanya revenue or margin decline.
